author: reek
body: FactLog is the on-disk shape of the fact log, in one place, so that the kernel writer and the compiler reader cannot drift apart. It is the chapter that exists BECAUSE a divergence once made a work read back as garbage, and until now nothing executed any of it: the compiler reaches it through FactDisk from `opening.codex`, DiskFacts and AppPersist write through it, and no test had ever asked whether a field reader reads the field its own constant names.

author: reek
body: The decoders are checked twice, deliberately. First against explicit literal bytes with a hand-computed answer, because a round trip through my own writer would share any byte-order assumption with the reader and could not see a swapped pair. Then as a round trip, which is what catches an offset the two halves disagree about. The first is the oracle, the second is the consistency check, and they answer different questions.

author: reek
body: The magic is asserted in both directions. Packed the way DiskFacts packs it -- one CCE code point per byte -- it must verify; with a single byte corrupted it must NOT, because a magic check that always answers yes is the function that always answers the same thing.

author: reek
body: A u64 whose top byte has the high bit set. Two's complement makes this negative, which is what a 64-bit machine word does and is worth pinning so nobody reads a negative timestamp as a decoder fault.

author: reek
body: The offsets must not overlap and must sit inside the header. Printed as numbers so a reader can check the layout prose against the constants without recomputing the widths.

author: reek
body: A byte-order fault IS visible to the round trip, because the writer is little-endian by construction: making fl-u16 big-endian moves both this chapter's `u16` line and the `kind` field. Two different faults, two different instruments.
